sanskrit: tad adbhutatamaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvāgastyasya rāghavaḥ gauravād vismayāc caiva bhūyaḥ praṣṭuṃ pracakrame
english: Having heard that most wondrous speech of Agastya, the Rāghava, out of both reverence and amazement, began to inquire further.

sanskrit: bhagavaṃs tad vanaṃ ghoraṃ tapas tapyati yatra saḥ śveto vaidarbhako rājā kathaṃ tad amṛgadvijam
english: "Blessed one, that dreadful forest where Śveta, the king of Vidarbha, practises austerities — how did it come to be devoid of deer and birds?

sanskrit: niḥsattvaṃ ca vanaṃ jātaṃ śūnyaṃ manujavarjitam tapaś cartuṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: That forest has become utterly lifeless, empty, and abandoned by men; yet he entered it to perform ascetic practice. I desire to hear the truth of this."

sanskrit: rāmasya bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā kautūhalasamanvitam vākyaṃ paramatejasvī vaktum evopacakrame
english: Having heard Rāma's words filled with curiosity, that supremely resplendent one began to speak.

sanskrit: purā kṛtayuge rāma manur daṇḍadharaḥ prabhuḥ tasya putro mahān āsīd ikṣvākuḥ kulavardhanaḥ
english: "Long ago, Rāma, in the Kṛta age, there was the lord Manu, wielder of the rod of punishment. His great son was Ikṣvāku, the increaser of the lineage.

sanskrit: taṃ putraṃ pūrvake rājye nikṣipya bhuvi durjayam pṛthivyāṃ rājavaṃśānāṃ bhava kartety uvāca ha
english: Placing that son in the ancestral kingdom on earth, that unconquerable realm, he said: 'Be the founder of royal lineages upon the earth.'

sanskrit: tatheti ca pratijñātaṃ pituḥ putreṇa rāghava tataḥ paramasaṃhṛṣṭo manuḥ punar uvāca ha
english: And that was assented to by the son, pledging 'so be it' to his father, O Rāghava. Then Manu, greatly delighted, spoke again.

sanskrit: prīto 'smi paramodārakartā cāsi na saṃśayaḥ daṇḍena ca prajā rakṣa mā ca daṇḍam akāraṇe
english: 'I am pleased; you are a doer of the most excellent deeds — of this there is no doubt. Protect the subjects by the rod of chastisement, but do not apply the rod without cause.'

sanskrit: aparādhiṣu yo daṇḍaḥ pātyate mānaveṣu vai sa daṇḍo vidhivan muktaḥ svargaṃ nayati pārthivam
english: 'The punishment that is inflicted upon erring men, when it is administered lawfully and duly, leads the king to heaven.'

sanskrit: tasmād daṇḍe mahābāho yatnavān bhava putraka dharmo hi paramo loke kurvatas te bhaviṣyati
english: 'Therefore, O mighty-armed one, be diligent in the matter of the rod of punishment, my son; for in so doing the highest dharma in the world will accrue to you.'

sanskrit: iti taṃ bahu saṃdiśya manuḥ putraṃ samādhinā jagāma tridivaṃ hṛṣṭo brahmalokam anuttamam
english: Having thus instructed his son at length with composure, Manu departed joyfully to the triple heaven, to the unsurpassed world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: prayāte tridive tasminn ikṣvākur amitaprabhaḥ janayiṣye kathaṃ putrān iti cintāparo 'bhavat
english: After Manu had departed to heaven, the boundlessly radiant Ikṣvāku became absorbed in the thought: 'How shall I beget sons?'

sanskrit: karmabhir bahurūpaiś ca tais tair manusutaḥ sutān janayām āsa dharmātmā śataṃ devasutopamān
english: By various and manifold acts, that son of Manu, righteous in soul, begot one hundred sons resembling the sons of gods.

sanskrit: teṣām avarajas tāta sarveṣāṃ raghunandana mūḍhaś cākṛtividyaś ca na śuśrūṣati pūrvajān
english: Of all of them the youngest, dear child, O Delight of the Raghu line, was foolish, unlearned, and did not serve his elders obediently.

sanskrit: nāma tasya ca daṇḍeti pitā cakre 'lpatejasaḥ avaśyaṃ daṇḍapatanaṃ śarīre 'sya bhaviṣyati
english: His father gave him the name Daṇḍa, that one of little lustre, saying: 'Surely the falling of the rod of punishment upon his body will come to pass.'

sanskrit: sa paśyamānas taṃ doṣaṃ ghoraṃ putrasya rāghava vindhyaśaivalayos madhye rājyaṃ prādād ariṃdama
english: Seeing that dreadful fault in his son, O Rāghava, O Subduer of Foes, Ikṣvāku gave him a kingdom between the Vindhya and the Śaivala mountains.

sanskrit: sa daṇḍas tatra rājābhūd ramye parvatarodhasi puraṃ cāpratimaṃ rāma nyaveśayad anuttamam
english: Daṇḍa became king there on that beautiful mountain terrain, and he founded a matchless, superb city, O Rāma.

sanskrit: purasya cākaron nāma madhumantam iti prabho purohitaṃ cośanasaṃ varayām āsa suvratam
english: He gave the city the name Madhumanta, O lord, and he chose the virtuous Uśanas as his royal chaplain.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa rājā tad rājyaṃ kārayat sapurohitaḥ prahṛṣṭamanujākīrṇaṃ devarājyaṃ yathā divi
english: Thus that king governed his kingdom together with his chaplain, thronged with joyful people, like the kingdom of the gods in heaven.

sanskrit: etad ākhyāya rāmāya maharṣiḥ kumbhasaṃbhavaḥ asyām evāparaṃ vākyaṃ kathāyām upacakrame
english: Having narrated this to Rāma, the great seer born of the water-jar proceeded in this same tale to speak another word.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa daṇḍaḥ kākutstha bahuvarṣagaṇāyutam akarot tatra mandātmā rājyaṃ nihatakaṇṭakam
english: Then that Daṇḍa, O descendant of Kākutstha, that dull-minded one, ruled his kingdom there for many thousands of years, with its enemies subdued.

sanskrit: atha kāle tu kasmiṃś cid rājā bhārgavam āśramam ramaṇīyam upākrāmac caitre māsi manorame
english: Then at a certain time, the king approached the charming hermitage of Bhārgava in the pleasant month of Caitra.

sanskrit: tatra bhārgavakanyāṃ sa rūpeṇāpratimāṃ bhuvi vicarantīṃ vanoddeśe daṇḍo 'paśyad anuttamām
english: There Daṇḍa saw the daughter of Bhārgava, incomparable in beauty upon the earth, wandering in a secluded part of the forest, that most excellent one.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā tāṃ sudurmedhā anaṅgaśarapīḍitaḥ abhigamya susaṃvignaḥ kanyāṃ vacanam abravīt
english: That one of very dull wit, seeing her and smitten by the arrow of the bodiless god of love, approached her in great agitation and spoke these words to the maiden.

sanskrit: kutas tvam asi suśroṇi kasya vāsi sutā śubhe pīḍito 'ham anaṅgena pṛcchāmi tvāṃ sumadhyame
english: 'From where are you, O fair-hipped one? Whose daughter are you, O auspicious one? Tormented by the bodiless god, I ask you, O slender-waisted one.'

sanskrit: tasya tv evaṃ bruvāṇasya mohonmattasya kāminaḥ bhārgavī pratyuvācedaṃ vacaḥ sānunayaṃ nṛpam
english: To him speaking thus, that lustful one maddened by delusion, the daughter of Bhārgava replied to the king with these gentle, conciliatory words.

sanskrit: bhārgavasya sutāṃ viddhi devasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ arajāṃ nāma rājendra jyeṣṭhām āśramavāsinīm
english: 'Know me as the daughter of Bhārgava, that divine one of unwearied actions; I am the eldest, called Arajā, dwelling in the hermitage, O king of kings.'

sanskrit: guruḥ pitā me rājendra tvaṃ ca śiṣyo mahātmanaḥ vyasanaṃ sumahat kruddhaḥ sa te dadyān mahātapāḥ
english: 'My father is your elder and teacher, O king of kings, and you are a pupil of that great-souled one; he is a great ascetic who, when angered, would bring very great calamity upon you.'

sanskrit: yadi vātra mayā kāryaṃ dharmadṛṣṭena satpathā varayasva nṛpa śreṣṭha pitaraṃ me mahādyutim
english: 'If anything is to be done with me in a righteous manner, on the proper path, then, O best of kings, seek my father's consent — that one of great radiance.'

sanskrit: anyathā tu phalaṃ tubhyaṃ bhaved ghorābhisaṃhitam krodhena hi pitā me 'sau trailokyam api nirdahet
english: 'Otherwise a dreadful consequence would befall you; for my father in his wrath could burn up even the three worlds.'

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇām arajāṃ daṇḍaḥ kāmaśarārditaḥ pratyuvāca madonmattaḥ śirasy ādhāya so 'ñjalim
english: Thus addressed by Arajā, Daṇḍa, pierced by the arrow of desire, intoxicated with passion, replied, placing his joined hands upon his head.

sanskrit: prasādaṃ kuru suśroṇi na kālaṃ kṣeptum arhasi tvatkṛte hi mama prāṇā vidīryante śubhānane
english: 'Show me favour, O fair-hipped one; you should not waste the moment. On your account my very life is being torn asunder, O one of auspicious face.'

sanskrit: tvāṃ prāpya hi vadho vāpi pāpaṃ vāpi sudāruṇam bhaktaṃ bhajasva māṃ bhīru bhajamānaṃ suvihvalam
english: 'Even death or dreadful sin upon obtaining you — honour me who am devoted, O timid one, devoted and utterly overwhelmed.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ dorbhyāṃ gṛhya balād balī visphurantīṃ yathākāmaṃ maithunāyopacakrame
english: Having spoken thus to the maiden, that mighty one seized her by force with his arms, and as she struggled, he proceeded to violate her according to his desire.

sanskrit: tam anarthaṃ mahāghoraṃ daṇḍaḥ kṛtvā sudāruṇam nagaraṃ prayayau cāśu madhumantam anuttamam
english: Having committed that great outrage, most terrible and cruel, Daṇḍa quickly went back to his superb city of Madhumanta.

sanskrit: arajāpi rudantī sā āśramasyāvidūrataḥ pratīkṣate susaṃtrastā pitaraṃ devasaṃnibham
english: And Arajā too, weeping, waited in great terror not far from the hermitage for her father, that one resembling a god.

sanskrit: sa muhūrtād upaśrutya devarṣir amitaprabhaḥ svam āśramaṃ śiṣya vṛtaḥ kṣudhārtaḥ saṃnyavartata
english: After a short while the divine seer of boundless radiance, accompanied by his disciples, hungry and afflicted, returned to his own hermitage.

sanskrit: so 'paśyad arajāṃ dīnāṃ rajasā samabhiplutām jyotsnām ivāruṇagrastāṃ pratyūṣe na virājatīm
english: He saw Arajā, dejected, covered with dust, like moonlight obscured by the red glow of dawn, no longer shining.

sanskrit: tasya roṣaḥ samabhavat kṣudhārtasya viśeṣataḥ nirdahann iva lokāṃs trīñ śiṣyāṃś cedam uvāca ha
english: Wrath arose in him, especially since he was afflicted with hunger, as if burning up the three worlds, and he spoke these words to his disciples.

sanskrit: paśyadhvaṃ viparītasya daṇḍasyāviditātmanaḥ vipattiṃ ghorasaṃkāśāṃ kruddhām agniśikhām iva
english: 'Behold the calamity of the perverted Daṇḍa who has not known his own self — terrible to behold, like an enraged tongue of fire.'

sanskrit: kṣayo 'sya durmateḥ prāptaḥ sānugasya durātmanaḥ yaḥ pradīptāṃ hutāśasya śikhāṃ vai spraṣṭum icchati
english: 'Destruction has come upon this evil-minded, wicked-souled one together with his retinue — he who desires to touch the blazing flame of the sacred fire.'

sanskrit: yasmāt sa kṛtavān pāpam īdṛśaṃ ghoradarśanam tasmāt prāpsyati durmedhāḥ phalaṃ pāpasya karmaṇaḥ
english: 'Because he has committed such a dreadful-to-behold sin, therefore that dull-minded one shall reap the fruit of his sinful deed.'

sanskrit: saptarātreṇa rājāsau sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ pāpakarmasamācāro vadhaṃ prāpsyati durmatiḥ
english: 'Within seven nights that king, that evil-minded one, doer of sinful deeds, together with his servants, army, and conveyances, shall meet his death.'

sanskrit: samantād yojanaśataṃ viṣayaṃ cāsya durmateḥ dhakṣyate pāṃsuvarṣeṇa mahatā pākaśāsanaḥ
english: 'The kingdom of this evil-minded one, a hundred yojanas in every direction, shall be burnt up by the great rain of dust sent by the Chastiser of Pāka.'

sanskrit: sarvasattvāni yānīha sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca mahatā pāṃsuvarṣeṇa nāśaṃ yāsyanti sarvaśaḥ
english: 'All beings here, both the stationary and the moving, shall entirely perish by the great rain of dust.'

sanskrit: daṇḍasya viṣayo yāvat tāvat sarvasamucchrayaḥ pāṃsubhuta ivālakṣyaḥ saptarātrād bhaviṣyati
english: 'The entirety of Daṇḍa's kingdom shall become invisible as if turned to dust within seven nights.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā krodhasaṃtapas tam āśramanivāsinam janaṃ janapadānteṣu sthīyatām iti cābravīt
english: Having spoken thus, burning with wrath, he said to the people dwelling in that hermitage: 'Let them remain at the borders of the realm.'

sanskrit: śrutvā tūśasano vākyaṃ sa āśramāvasatho janaḥ niṣkrānto viṣayāt tasya sthānaṃ cakre 'tha bāhyataḥ
english: Having heard the word of Uśanas, those people dwelling in the hermitage departed from his kingdom and took up residence outside it.

sanskrit: sa tathoktvā munijanam arajām idam abravīt ihaiva vasa durmedhe āśrame susamāhitā
english: Having spoken thus to the assembly of sages, he said to Arajā: 'Remain here, O one of lovely limbs, in the hermitage, with a composed mind.'

sanskrit: idaṃ yojanaparyantaṃ saraḥ suruciraprabham araje vijvarā bhuṅkṣva kālaś cātra pratīkṣyatām
english: 'This lake, extending a yojana in compass, of most lovely radiance, enjoy it, O Arajā, free from grief, and let the time be awaited here.'

sanskrit: tvatsamīpe tu ye sattvā vāsam eṣyanti tāṃ niśām avadhyāḥ pāṃsuvarṣeṇa te bhaviṣyanti nityadā
english: 'And whatever beings come to dwell near you on that night, they shall be forever exempt from destruction by the rain of dust.'

sanskrit: ity uktvā bhārgavo vāsam anyatra samupākramat saptāhād bhasmasādbhūtaṃ yathoktaṃ brahmavādinā
english: Having spoken thus, Bhārgava went to take up residence elsewhere. Within seven days it was reduced to ashes, as had been declared by that speaker of sacred truth.

sanskrit: tasyāsau daṇḍaviṣayo vindhyaśaivalasānuṣu śapto brahmarṣiṇā tena purā vaidharmake kṛte
english: That kingdom of Daṇḍa on the ridges of the Vindhya and Śaivala mountains was cursed long ago by that brahmarṣi when that transgression of dharma was committed.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti kākutstha daṇḍakāraṇyam ucyate tapasvinaḥ sthitā yatra janasthānam atho 'bhavat
english: 'From that time forward, O descendant of Kākutstha, it is called the Daṇḍaka forest; where ascetics dwelt, and where there was Janasthāna.'

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ yan māṃ pṛcchasi rāghava saṃdhyām upāsituṃ vīra samayo hy ativartate
english: 'All that you asked of me, O Rāghava, has been told. The time for performing the twilight devotion passes, O hero; it must not be neglected.'

sanskrit: ete maharṣayaḥ sarve pūrṇakumbhāḥ samantataḥ kṛtodako naravyāghra ādityaṃ paryupāsate
english: 'All these great seers with their water vessels filled stand on all sides; having performed the water rite, they attend upon the sun, O tiger among men.'

sanskrit: sa tair ṛṣibhir abhyastaḥ sahitair brahmasattamaiḥ ravir astaṃ gato rāma gacchodakam upaspṛśa
english: 'Attended upon by those seers together, those best of brahman-knowers, the sun has set, O Rāma; go and touch the water.'"
